title: The Empty Spot at Work Day

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager has missed the last four shared work days, and people are grumbling: hear them out, or ask around first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every few days, the whole village spends a morning on shared work: clearing paths, mending the storehouse, carrying water to the gardens. (subject) hasn't turned up for the last four. (friend) has noticed, and so have others, and there's grumbling. The council has asked (subject) to come and explain.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) explains that (fisher), the night fisher, is resting an injured ankle, so (subject.he/she) has been doing the night fishing alone all week, and sleeping through the mornings. Nobody knew. The grumbling stops. (friend) says (friend.he/she) is sorry for complaining, and the council asks two others to share the night fishing, so that (subject) can get some sleep.

text_only.reason: health or an injury talked about in the story; nobody's health changes -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The council asks around before (subject) arrives. Several people have seen (subject) paddling out every night and coming back at dawn with fish; nobody connected it with the empty spot at work day. By the time (subject) gets there, the council already knows, and simply thanks (subject.him/her). The next morning (friend) brings (subject.him/her) breakfast, which is a kind of apology.
